title: Accuracy of a month-3 transition self-rating for identifying new graduate nurses who leave within 12 months of hire: a single-site diagnostic accuracy study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the sensitivity and specificity of a month-3 Transition Check score of 30 or below for separation from the hospital within 12 months of hire. Design: diagnostic accuracy study in four residency intakes, October 2026 to October 2027. Reference standard: separation date in human resources records, ascertained blind to the score. Results and conclusions will be written after the last reference-standard extract.
introduction: One in five new graduate nurses leaves the hospital within a year of hire. A month-3 self-rating is already collected, and one external study suggests it identifies most later leavers while flagging many who stay. The hospital needs a local estimate before it ties a mentoring booster to the score.
methods: All residents attending the month-3 seminar are eligible. The cut-off of 30 or below was fixed in advance. Separation dates are released by a human resources analyst who does not see the scores, and transfers between units count as staying. Sensitivity and specificity are reported with Wilson intervals and predictive values at the local separation rate.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the STARD flow diagram, the 2 by 2 table, sensitivity and specificity with intervals, the ROC curve and predictive values.
discussion: The discussion will compare local accuracy with the external estimate, weigh how many flagged residents would stay anyway, and state whether the cut-off can target the booster.
limitations: Single site; residents who leave before month 3 are untested; about 56 separations limit precision.
conclusion: To be written after the analysis; it will be limited to the accuracy of this cut-off in this hospital.
summary: STARD-structured draft with results left empty until the reference-standard data exist.
